title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
The failure here is a match treated as an identification. License plate cameras flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, and deputies stopped a car they believed was that Camaro, even though neither the deputies nor the helicopter could read its plates. The alert was a lead about a vehicle somewhere in the area, and it was acted on as though it named the car in front of them. The stop escalated to at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs before anyone established the car was not the stolen one.

Catching this would have required a confirmation step between the camera alert and an armed stop. Reading the plate, or otherwise verifying the vehicle before treating its occupants as suspects in aggravated robberies, is the check that was missing. The gap sits at the handoff from a camera system's output to a field decision made under time pressure, where the alert carried the weight of a positive identification without any of its certainty.

What is not established is whether department procedures were followed, which the sheriff's office says supervisors will review against body-worn camera footage. The account of a deputy threatening to shoot and pushing one of the men is his allegation, and no finding has been made on it. The men were told how to file complaints with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies stopped two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, after mistaking their Camaro for a stolen car. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter surrounded them. Deputies drew guns and handcuffed them. Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot and kill him, leaving cuts and scrapes. The deputies thought the car was stolen because license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a similar car, but deputies and the helicopter could not read its plates, so they called backup.

After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. The sheriff's office said supervisors, including the district captain and shift lieutenants and sergeants, will review body-worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
